artworks.title: La Presse réactionnaire cherchant en vain...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a woman in classical drapery standing on a chariot holding a flag with the word "ITALIA" written on it. Beside the chariot, another female figure is depicted grasping a bar labeled "Insurrection de Palerme." The wheel of the chariot is marked with the word "MONDE."

artworks.title: C'est dommage que ma chasse a moi soit fermée
artworks.description: The image shows two figures. One figure is in the foreground with exaggerated facial features, wearing a uniform-like outfit with a helmet and holding the arms crossed over the chest. The other figure is in the background, aiming a rifle upwards. Additionally, birds are flying in the sky, and there is text at the top with a French caption below.

artworks.title: J'ai beau laver, l'ancienne couleur...
artworks.description: The image shows a person from the back, standing with their arms lifted and holding a cloth stretched between their hands. The person has neatly styled hair tied at the back, and is wearing a long, dark garment. They stand next to a wooden washtub filled with water. The cloth they are holding displays the words "PREMIER DRAPEAU." The background is simplistic.

artworks.title: Mars sans carême
artworks.description: The image depicts a seated person at a table with exaggerated features. They are reaching upward to drop coins into their mouth. The person wears a dress and sits amidst a pile of coins, a bag labeled "0000," and other objects. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Je vous en prie, rentrez dans votre boite...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a caricature scene involving a surprised individual. The image depicts a startled figure seated on a bench, with exaggerated, wide-eyed features and a distressed posture. They wear a large, floppy hat with a protruding crescent shape. Facing this figure is another character, draped in flowing garments, who appears to lean back, raising their hands. This character’s head is adorned with a cap labeled 'EUROPE'. The style is typical of 19th-century satirical illustrations, characterized by bold, expressive lines and dramatic contrasts.

artworks.title: Difficile à faire paraitre svelte
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure labeled "BUDGET" interacting with a tailor. The figure is depicted as large and round, wearing ill-fitting clothing. The figure appears resistant while the tailor is seen struggling to measure or fit the figure. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of political cartoons.

artworks.title: La France se préparant a passer...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a woman in a classical gown and crown holding a measuring stick. In front of her is a line of people with elongated heads just hovering over the measuring line. The people are drawn in a caricatured style, with expressions of nervousness or eagerness. The drawing uses strong lines and shading to create a satirical tone, contrasting the composed classical figure with the distorted figures in line.

artworks.title: Va te faire achever pour moi
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures interacting in an arid landscape. One figure is standing, wearing a robe and a large headdress, while the other is seated, holding a staff. The staff is held by both figures. In the background, "ROME" is written, and near the seated figure, "FRANCE" is inscribed on a shield. The drawing is characterized by strong black lines and stylized forms.

artworks.title: Utilisant les loisirs...
artworks.description: There is a drawing of a figure sharpening a sword with a grindstone. The image depicts a caricature-like character engaged in the act of sharpening a long sword. The character is bent over the grindstone, focused on its task. Opposite to the character, there are posters on a wall with the word "CANDIDAT" visible. The setting appears to be an indoor space with subtle shading indicating depth and the wooden structure. Shadows are used to give a sense of dimension to the scene.

artworks.title: Leur Mané, Thecel, Pharès
artworks.description: This is a drawing of several figures around a table reacting to a bright, round light source with the word 'République' inscribed within it. The light emits rays that fill the right half of the drawing. The figures are caricatured, with exaggerated features and postures, and appear contemplative or in shock. The scene likely conveys a critical or satirical tone related to social or political themes.

artworks.title: Les arènes législatives
artworks.description: This is a drawing of skeletons with political terms written on them. The drawing shows several human skeletons lying side by side with words like "AMENDEMENTS", "RÉFORMES", "LIBERTÉS PROMISE", and "PROJETS DE LOI" inscribed on them. Above the skeletons, two figures are depicted engaged in laborious activities - one pushing a wheelbarrow up an incline, and another using a pickaxe in the background. The drawing conveys a theme related to forgotten or neglected political promises and processes. At the bottom, the words "Les arènes législatives ou Les ruines de la Chambre en 2870" suggest a critique of legislative decay or stagnation.

artworks.title: Le Prince de Hohenzollern...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a person facing a throne surrounded by a chaotic pile of elements. The figure stands at the left, backed by shadowy shapes, observing a throne that sits atop a tumultuous heap of indistinct forms, which appear to be people in various poses. The setting is monochromatic, using bold lines to emphasize the dramatic contrast between the upright figure and the disorderly mound beneath the throne. The throne itself is ornate and crowned. The drawing employs satirical elements, as indicated by the exaggerated features and the tension between the figure and the daunting climb to the throne.

artworks.title: L'appel de leurs réserves
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene with armored figures and distressed individuals. The image shows a confrontation between helmeted soldiers or guards and apprehensive unarmored individuals. One armored figure is holding a baton, while the unarmored individuals appear concerned and are trying to shield a smaller figure. In the background, there is an open landscape with a sign that reads "DUCHE DE BADE."

artworks.title: Trop étroit pour deux
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in regal clothing seated on a throne. The illustration shows two characters, both dressed in opulent, regal attire with respective crowns. The characters are drawn in an exaggerated, satirical manner. They are sitting closely together on a single throne. The style is indicative of a caricature, with exaggerated facial features and postures. The surrounding space gives an impression of being from a printed publication.

artworks.title: Le Barbe bleu Prussien...
artworks.description: This is an illustration showing a character with a long beard and sword, standing in a hall in front of an audience. The character has flowing hair and cloak. The audience is seated in rows in an arena or theater, seen through an arched doorway. The drawing has detailed linework, and the overall tone is both humorous and slightly sinister. There are inscriptions on the walls marking different chambers with dates.

artworks.title: Ce qu'on appelle le Royaume-Uni
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in a boxing stance. One figure is labeled "John Bull" and the other is labeled "Irlande." The drawing depicts caricatures of the two figures preparing to box. On the left is a burly figure labeled “John Bull,” a personification of England, while on the right stands a gaunt figure labeled "Irlande" next to a sign post bearing the same name, representing Ireland. The contrast between the two figures is stark, showing differences in physique and attire. The image is a satirical commentary on the relationship between England and Ireland, with the text below reading "Ce qu'on appelle le ROYAUME-UNI," which translates to "What is called the UNITED KINGDOM," implying a critical view on the dynamics within the union. The drawing style is detailed with visible line work, capturing exaggerated facial and body expressions to enhance the satire.

artworks.title: Irlande et Jamaique - Patience!...
artworks.description: The image displays an illustrated scene with three figures in monochromatic drawing. The central figure is a man standing with exaggerated facial features, wearing tattered clothing. Beside him, another man is bent over whispering in his ear. A third man stands behind them holding a long stick over his shoulder. The background shows outdoor shading, with no specific elements depicted apart from the ground. French text is printed at the top and bottom of the illustration.

artworks.title: La Balançoire politique...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a seesaw with two figures on either end above a structure labeled "BOURSE". The image depicts a caricature-style illustration where one figure on the left is drawn wearing a top hat and holding a sprig, while the figure on the right is dressed in a Roman soldier attire, wielding a sword. The seesaw is balanced on a pedestal or platform, labeled with the word "BOURSE". The drawing captures a balance or conflict, with the two characters symbolizing different forces. The interaction between the two figures is dynamic, portraying tension and playfulness simultaneously. The lines are bold and expressive.

artworks.title: Ah! ça... ils n'ont plus l'air de s'occuper de moi
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring an elegantly dressed figure standing beside an empty chair labeled "PRINCIPAUTE," with an ornate crown on top. In the background, there is a large crowd of people. The scene is bustling with dynamic figures and raised arms, creating an atmosphere of chaos or celebration. The drawing is executed with strong lines and shading, highlighting the foreground's detail in contrast to the more sketch-like representation of the crowd. The text at the bottom in French translates to a remark about the crowd no longer paying attention to the central figure.

artworks.title: Le Cid se mettant aussi en campagne...
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure in armor atop a horse surrounded by a crowd. The scene features a knight-like figure fully clad in ornate armor holding a long lance while riding a noble horse. The crowd is shown in the background with expressive gestures and faces, and there are elements of architecture indicating an urban setting. The emphasis is on the detailed design of the armor and the expressive faces of the crowd. The style suggests a satirical or allegorical representation, possibly inspired by historical or literary themes.

artworks.title: L'Ordre règne à la Jamaique
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures. One is a large man with glasses and a hat, dressed in a suit, sitting on top of a smaller figure. The smaller person is laying face down and partially concealed beneath the larger individual. Only their limbs and the side of their face are visible. The background features stylized plants or trees. The drawing has a satirical and exaggerated style, likely from the 19th century. It contains contrasting size and demeanor of the two figures. The artwork's title is "L'Ordre règne à la Jamaïque" (Order reigns in Jamaica).

artworks.title: Le supplice de tantale... eau comprise
artworks.description: The image shows a person standing in profile, hunched over with their head resting on their left hand. Their right hand is placed on a long object. The person is wearing a helmet with a spike on top and a dark uniform with visible seams and folds. The face shows shadows and highlights, with an elongated nose and a pronounced chin. The hair is obscured by the helmet. The setting appears to be heavy rain, suggested by diagonal lines. In the background, another figure stands in a similar pose, creating depth. The image is monochromatic with a framed border, set in an open space.

artworks.title: Les marches du nouveau trone d'Allemagne
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure standing confidently on steps made of other figures. The figure has a uniform and a high hat, posed triumphantly with a hand on their hip. The figures beneath them appear reclined, forming steps leading to an ornate, vacant chair implied to be a throne. The style is reminiscent of a political cartoon, using sharp lines, exaggerated features, and a monochrome palette to emphasize the critical nature of the subject matter. The composition suggests a critique of power and authority, using visual metaphor to convey exploitation or subjugation underneath an elevated position.

artworks.title: Comment Bismarck comprend l'unité allemande
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of figures in a carriage scene. The figures wear crowns and are packed into the carriage, which is being pulled by figures at the front. Inside the carriage, more figures with exaggerated royal attire are seated. The style is cartoonish with exaggerated features, emphasizing the satirical nature of the scene. The drawing may comment on political or social themes. Fine lines and hatching are used to give depth and texture to the image, typical of a 19th-century satirical illustration style.
